Hmmm. Why do you say that? It took about a week to get used to but since then I've been very happy with it, and feel it's much more comfortable than the standard, archaic layout that only made sense when typewriters existed.
Why do you say the standard layout only made sense for typewriters? (genuinely curious)

Mostly the stagger. Because of way typewriters work, no two keys could be at the exact same horizontal coordinate. Each key has a bar running from the actual key that you hit to the top of the typewriter where the paper is. This is why keyboards today have that row stagger. So Q, A, and Z aren't perfectly aligned, for example.

But given the way your fingers work, it makes a lot more sense to stagger the other way, or not at all. When you extend your finger, it goes up and down. Not left and right. And in today's keyboards, there's no bar running up. We have the ability to put keys wherever we want. The ideal setups are columnar stagger (like this board) or ortholinear (like the Planck).

Does that make sense? Not sure I explained it well.
Actually that makes a lot of sense. I'd never heard it explained like that before.
